title: Choosing a Narrator Voice and Speaking Speed (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Choosing a Narrator Voice and Speed
slides.notes: The voice is the first thing viewers judge in a narrated video. Here's how to choose a narrator voice and speed that let your content do the talking.

slides.title: Test voices with your own script
bullets: Match the voice to the audience
Pick a familiar accent where you can
Compare two or three, not twenty
slides.notes: Don't judge a voice on its sample sentence. Paste in a real paragraph with the hard bits, then pick the voice that's easiest to follow.

slides.title: Set the speed for the content
bullets: Dense material: a little slower than default
Policy and instructions: default or slightly slower
Social clips: default or slightly faster
slides.notes: Speed matters as much as the voice. Too slow feels patronising, too fast loses people. If captions flick past, slow down; if you want to skip, speed up.

slides.title: Write for the voice, not the page
slides.notes: A synthetic narrator reads exactly what you write. So 'Q3 rev. up 8%' becomes 'Revenue in the third quarter rose eight per cent.'

slides.title: Timing follows the speech
bullets: Each slide lasts as long as its narration
Set a minimum time per slide
No narration option for silent loops
slides.notes: Each slide stays up as long as its narration lasts. For quiet slides or silent loops, set a minimum time per slide so nothing flashes past.

slides.title: Hear your own deck read aloud
bullets: Choose a voice and speaking speed
slides.notes: On Pro, a.i. directs the video, timing each animated scene to your narration. Try Basic first, then hear your deck at powerpoint2vid.com.
